bpmNote: General dance-teaching range is 80-160; no hip-hop-specific band was verifiable (R1 §3, marked DOĞRULANMADI). This narrower band is our teaching choice for V1, not a sourced fact.

copyright.basis: Foundational party-dance vocabulary is the category the US Copyright Office 'commonplace movements' exclusion targets. Three precedents confirm step-level freedom: 2 Milly v. Epic, Ribeiro/'Carlton' registration refusal, Hanagami v. Epic (which concerned a full routine, not a step).
copyright.boundary: Isolated steps are low risk; copying one instructor's original long sequence verbatim is not. Combos in this style must be our own arrangement.

honesty.$comment: K10 (plan §22) in machine-readable form. NOTE the asymmetry with salsa_shines: this style currently grades NOTHING, and says so. Two references exist (hh_running_man, hh_roger_rabbit) but neither backs a graded lesson — see notMeasured for the measured reasons.
honesty.measuredNote: Empty on purpose. This style grades nothing today. hh_bounce now HAS a reference (3 teachers, 2026-08-04) and is still ungraded — see notMeasured; a built reference is not the same as a gradeable one, and conflating them is exactly what this block exists to prevent.
notMeasured: The Running Man — we have measured 4 independent teachers doing it, and we still will not grade it: what makes this step right or wrong is the timing of the ball and heel of the foot touching the floor, and toe landmarks are the least reliable points a single phone camera produces. We can show you the step; scoring it would be scoring our own noise.

The Roger Rabbit — reference built from 3 teachers, but they disagree about which way round the step is danced (mirrorConfident:false), so we cannot tell a mirrored performance from a wrong one. Shown, not graded, until more teachers settle it.

The Bounce — three independent teachers HAVE now been measured, and the step is still not graded, for a reason we only learned by measuring: those teachers agree with each other more closely than our own camera noise. 83% of the tolerance we would grade you against comes from that noise floor rather than from anything they actually disagree about; in the lessons we do grade, that share is 9-28%. The movement itself is detected fine — every dip clears the step's own thresholds. What we cannot honestly do is turn that into a number about you.
Groove, feel and musicality — a camera cannot see whether the music is in you. Taught throughout, never scored (plan §22).
Rock and Groove — the step definitions are described but not authored, so there is nothing for the camera to check.

demoOnlyReason.en: We measured three teachers doing this step, and the result was not the one we expected: they move so alike that the differences between them are smaller than what a phone camera can reliably resolve. A score here would mostly be measuring our own uncertainty rather than your bounce. So you get the step, the count and three teachers' versions of it — the number is the part we are leaving out, and we would rather say that than hand you a confident-looking one.

promotionPath.unblockedBy: a rebuild with >=6 independent teachers whose measured disagreement exceeds the 6.0 deg floor, bringing the median floor-derived share into the 9-28% band; the tier question reopens on that measurement, not on a judgement call

demoOnlyReason.en: This one we can teach but not grade, and the reason is specific: the Running Man works through the timing of your ball and heel touching the floor — that is what makes it look like running in place. Toe and heel points are the least reliable thing a phone camera tracks, so any score we gave you would mostly be measuring our own uncertainty. You get the step, the count and four teachers' versions of it; you don't get a number.

lessons.evidence: content/references/hh_running_man.json (4 instructors, provisional) + stepInventory.tierC_excluded[Running Man] — measurability tier C per content/SCHEMA.md: dependent on toe-ground contact timing, the documented weak point of markerless single-camera pose (R1 §7b)
lessons.k10Note: K10 applied as intended: 'ölçülemeyen hareket ELENMEZ, demo-only işaretlenir ve nedeni kullanıcıya söylenir'. Previously this step was only recorded as tierC_EXCLUDED, which read as 'dropped from the product' — it is not; it is dropped from SCORING. The harvest effort (4 instructors, richest source 12 cycles) becomes user-facing content instead of a shelved measurement.
lessons.demoOnlyClassBasis: The step's identity IS toe/heel contact timing, and toe landmarks are the least reliable points in markerless single-camera pose (R1 §7b, tier C). A better harvest does not fix a landmark-reliability limit — this stays taught-not-scored.

whyPermanent.en: What decides whether a Running Man is right is the timing of the ball and heel of your foot meeting the floor — a few hundredths of a second, at the two points a phone camera tracks worst. That is not a limitation we expect to out-wait: more teachers would not move those landmarks. If we ever score this step it will be because the measurement changed, not because we got more data.

demoOnlyReason.en: Groove is the part of hip-hop a camera is worst at and a mirror is best at. We teach it and stay out of your way.

lessons.demoOnlyClassBasis: Groove is what a camera is worst at and a mirror is best at. Not a measurement gap, a category difference.

whyPermanent.en: Groove is not a quantity a camera can see. Two dancers can produce almost the same joint angles and only one of them is grooving; the difference lives in the music and in you, not in the geometry we can measure. We teach it throughout and we will not put a number on it.

levels.unlockRuleNote: No unlock rule, deliberately. Every lesson in this level is either locked or demo-only, so there is no graded attempt to gate progression on. Writing a threshold here (the previous draft had onBeatRatio >= 0.7 + shapeScore >= 0.75 against hh_bounce) would have been a rule referencing a measurement this style cannot currently make — the exact class of silent-wrong this codebase keeps catching. Restore it when hh_bounce has a real reference.

levels.note: Drills named by the step definitions' own error taxonomy. None of them are scored and none of them wait for a reference: a drill is a correction you practise, not a performance we judge (K10).

demoOnlyReason.en: The bounce at half tempo, with the count said out loud. Most beginners either stand still to the music or arrive at the bottom on the 'and' instead of on the beat — both are much easier to feel slowly than to see at speed. Same movement, more time to notice where the bottom actually lands, and whether one knee is doing more work than the other.

whyPermanent.en: A drill is a correction, not a performance. There is no such thing as several teachers agreeing on the right way to do the bounce at half speed — the slow version exists to let you feel something, not to be judged. Grading it would mean grading a target we made up.

demoOnlyReason.en: Stand with your back lightly against a wall and bounce. The wall does the checking for you: if you are bending at the waist instead of the knees, your back leaves the wall and you feel it immediately. A deliberate forward-leaning groove is a real style choice — this drill is about noticing when the lean is happening by accident.

whyPermanent.en: The wall is the feedback here, not us. This drill is a way of checking yourself, and putting a score on it would replace the thing that actually teaches it — noticing your own back leaving the wall.

levels.unlockRuleNote: No unlock rule by design. Every lesson in this level is a drill and none of them are scored, so there is no judgement the app is allowed to make that could gate them — an unlock rule here would have to invent a threshold on measurements we deliberately do not take (M-F-04: a rule may only depend on judgements we actually make). Drills are open from the start, which is also what they are for: you reach for one when a lesson tells you what went wrong.

sourcedFrom: iampro — Beginner Hip Hop Dance Foundations (20 steps)
stepInventory.note: Two independent lists overlap at ~20 steps, which is decent evidence for a stable core vocabulary. What the research did NOT produce is a biomechanical description per step — see MEASUREMENT below. Tier assignment therefore stays 'unknown' for most entries; assigning a tier without knowing what the body actually does would be a guess dressed as a decision.

removedEntries.tombstoneNote: Kept as a dated record rather than deleted outright: the record outlives the source. A line that simply vanishes takes its correction with it, and the next survey would be free to re-assert the same thing.

errorTaxonomy.gap: R1's beginner-error list for this style is pedagogical advice ('skipping fundamentals', 'being impatient', 'analysing the music with your head'), not observable form faults. Those may be true and are useful lesson copy, but none of them can be seen by a camera. Every entry in a step's errors[] must bind to a landmark-measurable condition (content/SCHEMA.md), so this style's error taxonomy has to be built from movement description, not from the existing research pass.

shipGatesNote: Empty on purpose, and that is not the same as 'ready to sell': this style has no BLOCKING release gate (bpmRange is set, and its demo-only lessons work without any scoring), so nothing here holds it back. What holds it back from being useful is content — every lesson is locked or demo-only, which is what `status: demoOpen` says on the other (orthogonal) axis. M-F-130: the two axes are read separately.
